_readme: M0 spike field audit. One reader (Claude Code, 2026-09-13) over 10 documents.
These are NOT labels and must not be used as gold. They record whether each draft-schema field is
E = stated explicitly, I = requires inference from the text, A = absent from this document,
C = the document contradicts itself about it. 'evidence' is a short quote or pointer.
trigger_class is audited only as 'is the trigger event described' -- no class is assigned (DERIVE-01 open).

org.evidence: 'Cloudflare's network' in first sentence; also in HTML metadata

title.evidence: in <title>/<h1>, lost by article-scoped extraction; not in body text

occurred_at.evidence: prose: 'began ... at 11:20 UTC'; timeline table: 'Impact starts' 11:28; trigger change 11:05

affected_services.evidence: table: Core CDN, Turnstile, Workers KV, Dashboard, Email Security, Access

trigger_event.evidence: 'triggered by a change to one of our database systems' permissions' -> duplicate rows -> oversized feature file -> panic

contributing_factors.evidence: narrative only: query lacks db filter; 200-feature prealloc limit; unwrap() panic; no kill switch; debug tooling CPU; status-page coincidence misled responders

detection_method.evidence: 'first automated test detected the issue at 11:31 and manual investigation started at 11:32'

time_to_detect.evidence: 11:28 impact / 11:31 detection (3 min) -- or 11 min if 11:20 start is used

time_to_mitigate.evidence: two endpoints: 14:30 'main impact resolved', 17:06 'all services resolved'

blast_radius.evidence: qualitative only: 'majority of core traffic', 'worst outage since 2019'; 5xx chart with no numbers

remediation_actions.evidence: 4 bullets under 'Remediation and follow-up steps' (all future tense)

occurred_at.evidence: date explicit; time ambiguous: snapshot 17:20, load 19:00, wipe ~23:30 UTC; data-loss window 17:20-00:00

affected_services.evidence: GitLab.com database-backed features; repos/wikis unavailable but not lost; Enterprise/self-managed unaffected

trigger_event.evidence: engineer wiped PostgreSQL data dir on primary instead of secondary while rebuilding replication

contributing_factors.evidence: explicit 5-Whys chains for two problems (~13 whys); backups failing silently; DMARC-rejected cron mail; no ownership

detection_method.evidence: actor noticed own mistake 'a second or two after'; no enum value fits (self-detected operator action)

time_to_detect.evidence: 'a second or two' (relative, not a timestamp)

time_to_mitigate.evidence: 'down for about 18 hours'; restored Feb 1 17:00-18:00 UTC

blast_radius.evidence: 'roughly 5,000 projects, 5,000 comments and 700 new user accounts'; 6h data window

change_induced.evidence: trigger was a manual command, not a deploy/config change; boolean is ambiguous

title.evidence: 'Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region'

occurred_at.evidence: 'started at 11:48 PM PDT on October 19' -- spans two calendar dates; PDT not UTC

affected_services.evidence: DynamoDB, EC2, NLB, Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Connect, STS, IAM sign-in, Redshift, Support Center, + 'Refer to the event history for the full list' (open-ended)

trigger_event.evidence: 'latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system' between two DNS Enactors; no change

contributing_factors.evidence: spread across 6 service sections: stale plan-newer check; cleanup deleted active plan; DWFM congestive collapse with 'no established operational recovery procedure'; NLB health-check flapping; Lambda SQS poller; Redshift IAM dependency

detection_method.evidence: DynamoDB: 'Engineering teams ... were immediately engaged' (mechanism unstated); NLB sub-incident: 'Our monitoring systems detected this at 6:52 AM'

time_to_detect.evidence: 11:48 PM start; 'By 12:38 AM ... identified DynamoDB's DNS state as the source' is diagnosis, not detection

time_to_mitigate.evidence: many endpoints: DynamoDB 2:40 AM; NLB 2:09 PM; EC2 1:50 PM; event end 2:20 PM; Redshift Oct 21 4:05 AM

blast_radius.evidence: one region; per-service 'increased error rates'; no counts or percentages

change_induced.evidence: no: latent defect triggered by timing ('unusually high delays')

remediation_actions.evidence: one paragraph: DNS automation disabled worldwide; NLB velocity control; EC2 DWFM test suite; queue-based throttling

title.evidence: in metadata; body text starts with author name (title lost by extraction)

affected_services.evidence: 'US1, EU1, US3, US4, and US5 Datadog regions across all services' -- axis is region, not service

trigger_event.evidence: 'a security update to systemd was automatically applied to a number of VMs' -> systemd-networkd deleted Cilium routes

contributing_factors.evidence: labelled: 'The aggravating factor is...'; legacy update channel; default 06:00-07:00 window coupling regions; quorum-based stores; cloud autoscaler replacing nodes

detection_method.evidence: 'first alerted to the issue by our internal monitoring, three minutes after the trigger'

time_to_mitigate.evidence: three endpoints: web 09:13 UTC; all services Mar 9 08:58; fully resolved Mar 10 06:25 after backfill

blast_radius.evidence: 'tens of thousands of nodes'; 5 regions; no customer counts

change_induced.evidence: yes, but the change was an OS auto-update nobody at Datadog initiated

remediation_actions.evidence: disabled legacy channel; systemd-networkd config; audited channels; lessons: degraded mode, chaos scale, status comms

title.evidence: in metadata ('October 21 post-incident analysis'); body starts with byline

affected_services.evidence: webhooks, GitHub Pages builds, stale/inconsistent data; 'portions of our platform were not affected'

trigger_event.evidence: 'routine maintenance work to replace failing 100G optical equipment' -> 43s partition -> Orchestrator cross-region failover

contributing_factors.evidence: narrative: Orchestrator allowed cross-region promotion; app can't tolerate cross-country latency ('major contributing factor'); remote backups slow; replication catch-up nonlinear; webhook TTL

detection_method.evidence: 'Our internal monitoring systems began generating alerts' at 22:54 UTC

time_to_mitigate.evidence: '24 hours and 11 minutes' explicit; intermediate: primaries back 11:12, failover 16:24, green 23:03

blast_radius.evidence: 'over five million hook events and 80 thousand Pages builds queued'; '~200,000 webhook payloads ... dropped'; '954 writes' example -- queue counts, not user counts

change_induced.evidence: physical maintenance is a change but not a deploy/config change

remediation_actions.evidence: Orchestrator config; new status page; active/active/active; fault injection; reconciliation of 954-write class

title.evidence: 'External Technical Root Cause Analysis -- Channel File 291'

occurred_at.evidence: 'On July 19, 2024' -- date only; no time of day in this document

affected_services.evidence: 'Windows sensors' 7.11+ on customer hosts -- affected thing is customer machines, not a vendor service

trigger_event.evidence: two IPC Template Instances deployed; one used a non-wildcard 21st parameter -> out-of-bounds read

contributing_factors.evidence: numbered Findings 1-6 (compile-time validation, bounds check, test coverage, Content Validator logic, stress test scope, staged deployment)

detection_method.evidence: not discussed in the RCA (covered in the earlier PIR, which this document references)

time_to_mitigate.evidence: absent; only '~99% of Windows sensors are online' by July 29 (recovery, 10 days later)

blast_radius.evidence: host count is in the PIR, not here

remediation_actions.evidence: per-finding mitigations with done/planned dates (July 25, July 27, Aug 9, Aug 19)

title.evidence: page title is auto-generated: 'Multiple GCP products are experiencing Service issues.'; a descriptive title must be inferred

occurred_at.evidence: banner 'began at 2025-06-12 10:51'; mini report 'Incident Start: 10:49'; full report 'at ~10:45am PDT, a policy change was inserted'; code deployed May 29

affected_services.evidence: two different product lists in the same page (banner ~60, mini report ~90 + Workspace)

trigger_event.evidence: policy change with 'unintended blank fields' replicated globally -> null pointer -> Service Control crash loop; latent code from May 29

contributing_factors.evidence: prose: no error handling; no feature flag; instant global replication; no randomized exponential backoff (herd on Spanner); status page itself down

detection_method.evidence: 'Within 2 minutes, our Site Reliability Engineering team was triaging' -- mechanism not stated

time_to_mitigate.evidence: mini report 'Duration: 3 hours' / 'Incident End: 13:49'; banner 'ended at 18:18'; full report 'up to ~2h 40 mins' for us-central1; red-button done 'within 40 minutes'

change_induced.evidence: yes -- but two changes (May 29 code, June 12 policy data); which is 'the' trigger is a taxonomy decision

remediation_actions.evidence: 7 bullets in full report; 3 different bullets in mini report; change freeze

occurred_at.evidence: date only from title '2-22-22' and 'February 22 this year'; time 'Just after 6 a.m. Pacific Time'

affected_services.evidence: 'many users were unable to connect'; client boot API; single-product company

trigger_event.evidence: Consul agent upgrade (25% PBR step) -> memcached churn -> cache misses -> scatter-query overload cascade; author separates 'trigger' from 'cause'

contributing_factors.evidence: listed: 'performance bottlenecks, cascading failures, dependency on a warm cache, and changes as triggering events'; plus scatter query, Mcrib efficiency, client retries

detection_method.evidence: three simultaneous: 'user tickets', 'internal users experienced problems', 'engineering teams received pages or alerts' -- multi-valued

time_to_detect.evidence: trigger (PBR step) time not given; symptoms 'just after 6 a.m.'

time_to_mitigate.evidence: no end time or duration anywhere in the post

remediation_actions.evidence: prose: Consul rollout process changed; scatter query moved to sharded-by-channel table; Mcrib control-loop changes; query audit

org.evidence: Roblox; co-authored 'in collaboration with ... HashiCorp'; root cause is in HashiCorp's Consul/BoltDB -- two orgs

trigger_event.evidence: enabling Consul streaming on traffic-routing service + 50% more nodes the day before; 'root cause was due to two issues' (streaming contention, BoltDB freelist)

contributing_factors.evidence: summary bullets: single Consul cluster; circular telemetry dependency; 128-core NUMA worsened contention; cache bootstrap tooling; unhealthy node seen as open

detection_method.evidence: 'Vault performance was degraded and a single Consul server had high CPU load. Roblox engineers began to investigate' -- dashboard vs alert unstated

time_to_detect.evidence: anchor ambiguous: from trigger (10/27 14:00, ~24h) or from impact (players unaffected at 13:37; 50% drop at 16:35)

blast_radius.evidence: 'online players dropped to 50% of normal'; 50M daily users; 73 hours

change_induced.evidence: yes, but the change preceded impact by ~24h

remediation_actions.evidence: sections: telemetry, multi-AZ/DC, Consul sharding, bbolt upgrade, bootstrapping tools

org.evidence: Kubernetes test-infra / Prow -- an OSS project team, not a company

title.evidence: H1: 'February 8th, 2019 - Prow responding slow & Partial outage'

occurred_at.evidence: timeline: 13:20 PST deploy; 13:46 first log symptom; 16:04 noticed; chat-log appendix uses 2019-02-09 UTC

affected_services.evidence: prow.k8s.io, hook, test jobs, service cluster

trigger_event.evidence: auto-generated bump PR merged -> deploy; client refactor ignored literal 'default' cluster alias

contributing_factors.evidence: 'What went poorly' list (Friday, non-deterministic, no staging Prow); the 'no resource limits on service deployments' factor appears only in the chat-log appendix

detection_method.evidence: '@krzyzacy was poking around a PR, suddenly cats not working!' -- human noticed bot unresponsive; earlier 13:46 OOMKilled signal was seen and dismissed ('/shrug')

time_to_detect.evidence: 13:20 or 13:46 -> 16:04: 2h44m or 2h18m; depends on which signal counts

time_to_mitigate.evidence: 16:40 first rollback (ineffective); 17:25 correct rollback; 17:59 'confirmed Prow is healthy'

blast_radius.evidence: '600 pending pods', '225 unschedulable', '~5min delay' -- internal metrics, not users

remediation_actions.evidence: one vague action item ('be more careful ... more e2e tests, or ... staging Prow') + fix PR #11209
